definition: (Stochastic) variance reduction is an algorithmic approach to minimizing functions that can be decomposed into finite sums.
details: By exploiting the finite sum structure, variance reduction techniques are able to achieve convergence rates that are impossible to achieve with methods that treat the objective as an infinite sum, as in the classical Stochastic approximation setting. Variance reduction approaches are widely used for training machine learning models such as logistic regression and support vector machines as these problems have finite-sum structure and uniform conditioning that make them ideal candidates for variance reduction.

explainer.lead: An algorithmic approach to minimizing functions that decompose into finite sums, achieving convergence rates unreachable when the objective is treated as an infinite sum. It matters for training models whose loss is a sum over data points.

tiers.eli5: Instead of noisy one-sample guesses at the slope, you reuse past information so each step points more reliably downhill.
tiers.practitioner: Used to train finite-sum models such as logistic regression and support vector machines; the pitfall is that the finite-sum structure and uniform conditioning the methods rely on do not hold for every problem.
tiers.paperLevel: By exploiting finite-sum structure, variance reduction techniques attain convergence rates impossible under classical stochastic approximation, which treats the objective as an infinite sum.

explainer.example: Training a support vector machine, whose objective is a finite sum over training examples, with a variance-reduced optimizer.
